label: copy-phase echo of e/n near the end of the output
explanation: Very sparse feature (~0.02% of steps). 99% of activation mass is in the copy phase, at steps where the fed-back input is e (63% of mass) or n (27%), with a little on u/b. Almost every firing is on a repeated token (in_first=0), i.e. the copied echo, not the original occurrence. It fires on the last few outputs (to_go<=3), which means the first copy step for L=3-4 and the tail of the copy for L=8-9. It is almost silent for L=5-7 and never fires in the original phase. The predicate covers about 87% of activations and activation mass, but precision is under 1%: only a tiny fraction of copy-phase e/n echoes fire. The strongest activations are on e at the first copy step of short sequences when the next output is f (for example e f p <DEL> [e] f). That narrow case is about 70% precise but covers under 5% of activations. Output tokens f/j/n raise the firing rate. What decides which e/n echoes fire is not captured.
